why: A single left-to-right pass: add points[K] for every token cell and +1 whenever a token cell's left neighbour is also a token. No pattern beyond careful counting.
hints: Two separate contributions: the points of token cells, and the adjacent token pairs.
A pair (K-1, K) is counted once, when you are at K and both cells are 'T'.
pitfalls: Three tokens in a row make two pairs, not one (TTT gives +2).
Do not count a pair twice by also checking the right neighbour.
statement:
A board has N cells in a row, numbered 0 to N-1. You get an array points and a string tokens, both of length N. tokens[K] is 'T' if cell K holds a token and 'E' if it is empty.

Your score is:

  • points[K] for every cell K that holds a token, plus
  • 1 extra point for every pair of adjacent cells (K, K+1) that both hold tokens.

Return the total score.

Example: points = [3,4,5,2,3], tokens = "TEETT"

  • Token cells are 0, 3 and 4: 3 + 2 + 3 = 8.
  • Adjacent token pairs: (3,4) only, so +1.
  • Total: 9.
